items.title: Section: Rewards Given Only After Resentment Has Already Set In

items.zh: 云何名王猛利憤發？謂有國王，諸群臣等有小愆過、有少違越，便削封祿，奪去妻妾，或以重罰而刑罰之。如是名王猛利憤發。云何名王恩惠奢薄？謂有國王，諸群臣等供奉侍衛，雖極清淨，善稱其心，而以微劣軟言慰喻；頒賜爵祿、酬賞勳庸不能圓滿，不順常式。或損耗已、或稽留已、或推注已、或怨恨已。然後方與。如是名王恩惠奢薄。云何名王受邪佞言？若有國王，諸群臣等實非聰叡，有聰叡慢，貪濁偏黨，不閑憲式，情懷謀叛，不修善政，聽受信用如是輩人所進諫議，由此因緣，王務、財寶、名稱、善政並皆衰損。如是名王受邪佞言。云何名王所作不思不順儀則？謂有國王，不能究察、不審究察、不能思擇、不審思擇諸群臣輩，於彼彼務機密事中，不堪委任而委任之，堪委任者而不委任；
items.en: What is called a king's fierce, uncontrolled anger? A king who, when his ministers commit even the smallest fault or minor overstepping, strips their rank and salary, seizes their wives and concubines, or subjects them to severe punishment. This is called fierce, uncontrolled anger. What is called a king's sparing, stingy kindness? A king whose ministers serve him purely and to his genuine satisfaction, yet who offers only faint, feeble words of comfort, granting rank and reward for merit incompletely, contrary to custom, whether depleted, delayed, extracted through further labour, or given only once resentment has already arisen. This is called sparing, stingy kindness. What is called a king's heeding deceitful counsel? A king whose ministers, lacking real wisdom yet carrying an arrogant pretence of it, driven by greed and faction, unfamiliar with proper law, secretly plotting rebellion and governing poorly, are nonetheless trusted and heeded, his own governance, treasury, reputation, and administration all declining as a result. This is called heeding deceitful counsel. What is called a king's acting without thought and without regard for protocol? A king who neither investigates nor carefully considers his ministers, entrusting sensitive duties to the unfit while overlooking the fit.

items.zh: 堪驅役者而不驅役，不堪役者乃驅役之；應賞賚者而刑罰之，應刑罰者而賞賚之。又於群臣，不善安處先王儀則；由此群臣處大朝會，餘論未終發言間絕，不敬不憚而興諫諍，不如旨教而善奉行，不正安住王之教命。如是名王所作不思不順儀則。云何名王不顧善法？謂有國王，不信他世，亦不曉悟；由於他世不信不悟，便於當來善不善業、愛非愛果不能信解；不信解故，無有羞恥，隨情造作身語意業三種惡行，不能時時布施、修福、受齋、學戒。如是名王不顧善法。云何名王不知差別忘所作恩？謂有國王，於諸大臣、輔相、國師及群官等其心顛倒，不善了知忠信、伎藝、智慧差別。以不知故，非忠信所生忠信想，於忠信所非忠信想；無伎藝所生伎藝想，有伎藝所無伎藝想；於惡慧所生善慧想，於善慧所生惡慧想。彼由如是心顛倒故，於非忠信、無有伎藝、惡慧臣所敬重愛養，忠信、伎藝、善慧臣所反生輕賤。

items.title: Section: Forgetting the Old Servants Who Gave Their Whole Lives

items.zh: 又諸臣等年耆衰邁，曾於長夜供奉侍衛，知其無勢、無力、無勇，遂不敬愛，不賜爵祿、不酬其賞；設被陵蔑，捨而不問。如是名王不知差別忘所作恩。云何名王一向縱任專行放逸？謂有國王，於妙五欲一向沈沒、耽著嬉戲、愛樂受行，不能時時勗勵方便作所應作，勞賚群臣。如是名王一向縱任專行放逸。若有國王成就如是十種過失，雖有大府庫、有大輔佐、有大軍眾，而不可歸仰。大王當知！此十過失，初一是王種姓過失，餘九是王自性過失。
items.en: And ministers now aged and enfeebled, who once served him faithfully through long years of attendance, knowing they lack influence, strength, and vigour, are no longer cherished, granted rank or salary, or rewarded; should they be humiliated by others, they are abandoned and ignored. This is called failing to distinguish and forgetting kindness received. What is called a king's heedless self-indulgence? A king utterly sunk in the five exquisite pleasures, given to amusement and delight, unable to rouse himself to his own proper duties or reward his ministers. This is called heedless self-indulgence. Should a king possess these ten faults, though he has a great treasury, great ministers, and a great army, he does not deserve reliance. Great King, you should know that of these ten faults, the first is a fault of lineage, and the remaining nine are faults of character.

blocks.text: The rest of the ten faults. Each describes a kind of leader most people have worked under.

For a small fault, the minister loses pay: the point is the disproportion. Rewards are delayed until resentment has already set in. Master Cháng Bǎi: through greedy flatterers, the king's affairs, treasury, good name, and good ministers decline.

**Acting without thought.** The king does not examine his ministers: he entrusts secret matters to the unfit, works the unable, punishes those who deserve reward and rewards those who deserve punishment. His ministers interrupt one another at court and do not follow his commands. **Not caring for the good.** He does not believe in a next life, so has no shame, follows his impulses, and does not give, make merit, keep the observance, or train in precepts. **Not discerning.** He mistakes the disloyal for loyal, the unskilled for skilled, the foolish for wise; he honours the bad ministers and slights the good.
Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing them old and powerless, the king no longer cherishes retired ministers, and if others bully them he ignores it.
"Rewards given only after resentment has set in." Generosity that comes late has lost most of its value.

quiz.q: What is 猛利憤發, fierce anger?
options: a great fault receives a punishment that matches it under law
loud scolding with no punishment
a small fault brings loss of rank and salary, seizure of wives, or severe punishment
silent resentment never shown
quiz.why: The point is the disproportion between small fault and heavy penalty. Master Cháng Bǎi: for a small fault or minor overstepping, their pay is cut or taken away. §7's mild anger is the reverse, punishing according to the weight of the fault.

quiz.q: The English reads "A king whose ministers ... has his rank and salary stripped." What is wrong?
options: the subject slips: literally the king loses rank, but he is the one who punishes
nothing: the text says ministers strip a king of his rank, which links with lack of mastery
"stripped" should be "stolen"
"concubines" should not appear
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi makes clear that the ministers have the fault and lose their pay. Grammatically the English subject is "a king," so he seems to be stripped. §7's parallel, "does not entirely strip their rank and salary," has it right.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain giving a reward only after resentment?
options: the king himself resents the minister, so what he gives he soon takes back again
he delays until the minister has begun to complain and is close to losing his temper, and only then gives
the minister refuses it out of hatred
he scolds in public while giving
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: he keeps delaying until the other has started to complain and resent, sees that things are amiss, and only then gives. The resentment is the minister's, not the king's. The kindness is thin both in words and in timing.

quiz.q: What result of heeding deceitful counsel does the treatise state?
options: he is deposed at once and the flatterers seize the throne, since they plot rebellion
his affairs, treasury, reputation, and good governance all decline together
only wealth is lost, not reputation
only the next life suffers
quiz.why: The treatise lists four things that decline; it does not say the king is overthrown. Master Cháng Bǎi: through these greedy flatterers, the king's affairs, treasury, good name, and past good government all suffer. Honest counsel in §7 makes the same four flourish.

quiz.q: Where does Master Cháng Bǎi see the king failing to distinguish and forgetting kindness?
options: he keeps aged ministers in high office, unable to tell old from young
he miscounts the rewards
he no longer cherishes aged ministers, ignores their humiliation, and forgets those who once did him good
he forgets his ministers' names
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing them old and powerless, the king no longer cherishes the retired ministers, and if others bully them he ignores it. Such a king does not know the difference among ministers and forgets those who once gave him kindness.
